- Overestimate early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–2% for high-impact days.
- Underestimate late in the horizon when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust final 5–10 days upward by 0.5–1.5% to account for mean reversion bias.
- Avoid overshooting after sharp upward moves; cap forecast peaks at 1.5–2% below the immediate prior high.
- If sentiment remains flat (0.00) for 18+ days, reduce forecast volatility and shift mean toward recent 7-day average.
- When true outcome exceeds forecast by >1.5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid momentum overcorrection.
- For horizon >20 days, apply exponential decay weighting to recent data (e.g., 70% weight on last 5 days, 30% on prior 15) to reduce lagged bias.
